A full build downloads daily prices, corporate actions and company listings for every US common stock in the subscription, including delisted ones, and stores them locally.

criteria: Given an empty local store, when the researcher runs a full build, then afterwards the store holds prices, corporate actions and listings for every common stock the subscription lists, active and delisted.

nodes.title: An incremental build adds only trading days and corrections published since the last build.

criteria: Given a store built through date D, when the researcher runs an update after new data is published, then only data after D (and vendor corrections to earlier rows) is downloaded, and the earlier stored rows are unchanged except where corrected.
Given a vendor correction to an earlier row, when it is stored, then the earlier value is kept with the date it was replaced, so an as-of-D load still returns what was known on D.

nodes.title: Cleaning resolves duplicate rows, non-positive prices and missing trading days before storage.

criteria: Given a raw batch with a duplicated (stock, date) row, when it is cleaned, then exactly one row is stored and the duplicate is listed in the run report.
Given a price ≤ 0 or a missing trading day inside a stock's listed life, when it is cleaned, then the row is flagged (not filled with a zero return) and listed in the run report.

nodes.title: Every build ends with a validation report that passes or fails.

criteria: Given a completed build, when the report is produced, then it states counts of stocks, stock-days, delisted stocks and flagged rows, and the result of every check in XCHK and UNIV.
Given any check that fails, when the build finishes, then the run is marked failed and the loader refuses to treat it as the current dataset until the researcher accepts it.

nodes.title: An interrupted build can be resumed without starting over.

criteria: Given a build stopped part-way (network loss, laptop sleep), when the researcher reruns it, then it continues from the last completed batch and the final store equals one built without interruption.

nodes.title: For each trading date, the universe is the 1,000 US common stocks with the highest trailing dollar volume, measured over the previous 63 trading days.

criteria: Given trading date D, when the universe for D is requested, then it holds the 1,000 common stocks with the highest median daily dollar volume (price × shares traded) over the 63 trading days ending the day before D.
Given a stock with fewer than 63 trading days of history before D, when the universe for D is built, then it is ranked only once it has at least 63 days.

nodes.title: Universe membership on date D uses no data from D or later.

criteria: Given the universe for D, when any price, volume or listing published on or after D is changed, then the universe for D is unchanged.

nodes.title: Stocks that later delist stay in the universe on every date they qualified.

criteria: Given a stock that qualified on D and delisted after D, when the universe for D is requested, then the stock is in it, and its final return through delisting is part of the data.

nodes.title: If the data budget (or the data itself) can't support the dollar-volume universe, the universe falls back to S&P 500 membership as it was on each date.

criteria: Given the decision (made when the data source is checked) that the budget or data limits the dollar-volume universe, when the universe for D is requested, then it holds the stocks that were S&P 500 members on D, including those later removed or delisted.
Given a listing that is an ETF, ADR, preferred share, warrant, unit or fund, when the universe is built, then it is never included.

nodes.title: Daily total returns are compared with a second independent source for every universe stock it covers.

criteria: Given a completed build, when the cross-check runs, then for each universe stock-day both sources cover, the two daily total returns (dividends and splits included) are compared, and the report states the share of stock-days within 0.5% of each other.
Given the share within 0.5% is below 99%, when the build finishes, then the cross-check fails.

nodes.title: Every stock-day disagreeing by more than 2% is listed with a reason.

criteria: Given a stock-day whose returns differ by more than 2%, when the report is produced, then it appears with one reason: split, dividend, missing in one source, stale price, or unexplained.

nodes.title: Corporate actions are checked against the second source.

criteria: Given a split or dividend in the stored data, when the cross-check runs, then the report states whether the second source shows the same action within 1 trading day, and lists each mismatch.

nodes.title: Coverage gaps in the second source are reported, not treated as errors.

criteria: Given a stock the second source doesn't cover (often a delisted one), when the cross-check runs, then it is counted as "not covered", and the report states the share of universe stock-days covered.

nodes.title: The loader returns daily adjusted prices and total returns for a date range.

criteria: Given a date range, when the researcher loads prices, then each stock-day carries the close, the split-adjusted close and the total return including dividends.

nodes.title: The loader returns corporate actions for a date range.

criteria: Given a date range, when the researcher loads corporate actions, then every split, dividend, ticker change and delisting in that range is returned with its effective date.

nodes.title: A load can be restricted to the point-in-time universe.

criteria: Given a date range, when the researcher loads universe returns, then each date holds only the stocks in that date's universe, and stocks that later delisted are present on their qualifying dates.

nodes.title: A load as of date A returns only what was known on A.

criteria: Given as-of date A, when anything is loaded, then no row, correction or adjustment published after A is returned.
Given a stock-day with no trade, when it is loaded, then its return is marked missing, never filled with zero.

nodes.title: The loader only serves accepted builds.

criteria: Given the latest build failed validation and wasn't accepted, when the researcher loads, then the last accepted build is served and a warning names the failed one.

nodes.title: The exploratory analysis is run with the data-analysis skill on the accepted dataset.

criteria: Given an accepted build, when the analysis runs, then it is done with the data-analysis skill, given the universe returns from the loader, and it produces: universe size and delistings per year, missing-data share per year, return distribution and tails by year, and the eigenvalue spectrum of the correlation matrix per year.

nodes.title: The analysis results are saved with the build they came from and can be rerun.

criteria: Given the same accepted build, when the analysis is rerun, then it produces the same figures and numbers.

nodes.title: The analysis results can be viewed in the explorer app.

criteria: Given a saved analysis, when the researcher opens it in the app, then every figure and table is shown with the build it came from.

nodes.title: The researcher can view any stock's price and return history with its corporate actions marked.

criteria: Given a stock, when the researcher opens it, then its adjusted price and daily return are charted over its whole listed life, splits and dividends are marked on the chart, and a delisting is shown as the end of the series.

nodes.title: The researcher can view the universe on any date.

criteria: Given a trading date, when the researcher picks it, then the app lists that date's universe members with their trailing dollar volume rank, and how many joined and left since the previous month.

nodes.title: The researcher can view the cross-check results of any build.

criteria: Given a build, when the researcher opens its validation report, then every check's result and each listed disagreement with its reason is shown, and a disagreement opens both sources' series side by side.

nodes.title: The researcher can start a build or validation from the app and watch its progress live.

criteria: Given a running build, when the researcher watches it in the app, then progress (current step, batches done of total, errors so far) updates at least every 2 seconds without reloading the page.

nodes.title: Charts and layout are designed with the dataviz and frontend-design skills.

criteria: Given a new chart or screen, when it is built, then it follows the dataviz skill for the chart and the frontend-design skill for the screen, and reads correctly in light and dark themes.

nodes.title: A chart of one stock's full history appears within 1 second.

criteria: Given the full dataset, when the researcher opens any stock, then its chart is drawn within 1 second on the laptop.

nodes.title: Factor removal fits principal components of the window's universe returns and subtracts each stock's exposure to the top k components.

criteria: Given an estimation window and k, when factors are removed, then the residual returns for that window are the returns minus each stock's fitted exposure to the top k principal components of that window's returns.

nodes.title: Factor removal uses only data inside the estimation window.

criteria: Given a window ending on date E, when any return after E is changed, then the factors, exposures and residuals up to E are unchanged.
Given residuals for a later out-of-sample day, when they are produced, then they use the components and exposures fitted on the window before that day.

nodes.title: The number of components removed is chosen by a rule fixed before the run.

criteria: Given a run, when it starts, then k is either a fixed number or chosen per window by a stated rule (such as the count of eigenvalues above the random-matrix bound in DENO), and the choice is recorded with the run.

nodes.title: Removal reduces cross-stock correlation, and this is checked.

criteria: Given a window's raw and residual returns, when the check runs, then the mean absolute pairwise correlation of the residuals is lower than that of the raw returns, and both values are recorded.

nodes.title: Eigenvalues at or below the Marchenko–Pastur upper edge for the window's ratio of stocks to days are replaced by their average, and the ones above are kept.

criteria: Given a correlation matrix from T days and N stocks, when it is denoised, then every eigenvalue ≤ (1 + √(N/T))² (scaled by the fitted noise variance) is replaced by the mean of those eigenvalues, the eigenvalues above it are unchanged, and the result is rescaled to a unit diagonal.

nodes.title: The denoised matrix is a valid correlation matrix.

criteria: Given any denoised matrix, when it is checked, then it is symmetric, has a unit diagonal and has no negative eigenvalues.

nodes.title: Denoising recovers known structure on synthetic data.

criteria: Given a synthetic return panel with a known number of factors plus noise, when its correlation is denoised, then the count of kept eigenvalues equals the true factor count, and the denoised matrix is closer to the true correlation than the sample one.

nodes.title: The noise fit and the count of kept eigenvalues are recorded per window.

criteria: Given a denoising run, when it finishes, then each window's fitted noise variance, upper edge and number of kept eigenvalues are saved.

nodes.title: Each estimation window produces a sample, a shrinkage and a denoised covariance estimate of the universe returns.

criteria: Given an estimation window, when the estimates are made, then the sample covariance, a covariance shrunk toward a structured target with its intensity chosen from that window's data only, and a covariance rebuilt from the DENO correlation with the window's volatilities are all produced.

nodes.title: Estimators are ranked by the out-of-sample realized variance of the portfolios built from them.

criteria: Given the walk-forward schedule of HARN, when each estimator's covariance drives each portfolio method of PORT, then the realized variance of each portfolio over the following unseen period is recorded, and estimators are ranked per portfolio method by average realized variance.

nodes.title: The comparison of estimators is analysed with the data-analysis skill and tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill.

criteria: Given the out-of-sample realized variances, when the comparison is made, then the data-analysis skill characterises them (by period and market regime), and the null-hypothesis-testing skill tests each estimator against the sample covariance on the paired per-period variances; an estimator counts as better only if the null of no difference is rejected at 5% after correction for the number of comparisons.

nodes.title: Forecast accuracy of the risk estimate is reported alongside.

criteria: Given each portfolio and estimator, when results are recorded, then the predicted variance at rebalancing and the realized variance afterwards are both stored, with their ratio.

nodes.title: A minimum-variance portfolio is built from each covariance estimate.

criteria: Given a covariance estimate, when the portfolio is built, then its weights are fully invested, long-only, at most 5% per stock, and minimise predicted variance under those limits.

nodes.title: A risk parity portfolio is built from each covariance estimate.

criteria: Given a covariance estimate, when the portfolio is built, then each stock's contribution to predicted portfolio variance is equal to within 1%, and weights are fully invested and long-only.

nodes.title: A hierarchical risk parity portfolio is built from each covariance estimate.

criteria: Given a covariance estimate, when the portfolio is built, then stocks are clustered by correlation distance into a tree, ordered by it, and weights are split down the tree in inverse proportion to each branch's variance, fully invested and long-only.

nodes.title: Portfolios are compared out of sample on realized variance after costs, with turnover reported.

criteria: Given the walk-forward schedule of HARN, when each portfolio is held over its unseen period, then its realized variance, its return after the per-trade cost, and its turnover per rebalance are recorded.

nodes.title: An equal-weight portfolio of the universe is the simple baseline.

criteria: Given any comparison, when results are reported, then the equal-weight universe portfolio, under the same schedule and cost, is shown alongside.

nodes.title: The best classical portfolio is named as the benchmark for later stages.

criteria: Given the completed comparison, when it is recorded, then the portfolio (method and estimator) with the lowest out-of-sample realized variance after costs is saved as the stage benchmark, together with all the others.

nodes.title: Every run is pre-registered before it touches out-of-sample data.

criteria: Given a new comparison, when the researcher starts it, then the claim, the baseline, the metric, the test, the significance level and the final test period must be stated, and are saved and locked before any result is computed.
Given a registered run, when its settings are changed after results exist, then the harness records it as a new run, never as an edit of the old one.

nodes.title: Comparisons run walk-forward: estimate on a past window, then hold on the following unseen period.

criteria: Given a strategy, when it is run, then by default it is estimated on the previous 252 trading days and rebalanced every 21 trading days, and each period's result uses only data from before that period.

nodes.title: Learned models are trained, tuned and tested on separated periods with a gap.

criteria: Given a model whose labels look h trading days ahead, when data is split, then training, validation and test periods are in time order, and at least h trading days are removed between each pair so no label overlaps the next period.

nodes.title: A final test period is held back for each claim and used once.

criteria: Given a registered claim, when it is run on its final test period, then that run is the claim's verdict, and any later run on the same period is marked as a repeat.

nodes.title: Every comparison applies one per-trade cost and reports turnover.

criteria: Given any portfolio or agent, when its result is computed, then a cost of 10 basis points of traded value is charged on every trade, the cost is stated with the result, and turnover per rebalance and per year is reported.

nodes.title: Every claim is tested against chance with the null-hypothesis-testing skill.

criteria: Given a completed run, when its verdict is decided, then the null-hypothesis-testing skill is given the per-period results of the candidate and the baseline and the registered test; the claim passes only if the null of no improvement is rejected at the registered level, after correction for every candidate tried under that claim.

nodes.title: Every run's result is recorded, wins and losses alike.

criteria: Given any finished or abandoned run, when it ends, then its registration, results, test verdict and a written conclusion are saved, and a loss is recorded with the same detail as a win.
Given a recorded run, when it is rerun on the same accepted build with its recorded settings and random seeds, then it gives the same results.

nodes.title: The researcher can list every recorded run.

criteria: Given recorded runs, when the researcher opens the results list, then each run shows its stage, claim, date, verdict (passed, failed, abandoned) and baseline, and the list can be filtered by stage and verdict.

nodes.title: The researcher can open a run and see it against its baseline.

criteria: Given a run, when the researcher opens it, then its registration, the candidate's and baseline's out-of-sample results over time (variance, return after costs, turnover) and the test verdict are shown.

nodes.title: The researcher can compare runs side by side.

criteria: Given 2 to 6 runs, when the researcher selects them, then their out-of-sample results are charted on shared axes.

nodes.title: Each later stage's results appear without a new screen being built for them.

criteria: Given a run from stage S3 or S4 recorded through HARN, when the researcher opens the results list, then it appears and opens like any S2 run.

nodes.title: Each candidate feature is computed per universe stock-day from data up to that day's close.

criteria: Given a feature value for stock S on date D, when any data after D is changed, then the value is unchanged.

nodes.title: Each feature is registered with a definition before it is tested.

criteria: Given a new feature, when it is added, then its definition, inputs and lookback are recorded, and it counts toward the number of features tried from that moment.

nodes.title: Features are standardised across the stocks of each date's universe.

criteria: Given date D, when features are standardised, then each feature has mean 0 and standard deviation 1 across D's universe, using only D's universe members.

nodes.title: The initial candidate set covers price, volume and corporate-action information.

criteria: Given the first feature run, when the candidates are listed, then they include at least: past residual returns over several lookbacks, residual volatility, dollar volume and its change, and recent corporate actions.

nodes.title: The target is the next-period residual return from FACT.

criteria: Given date D, when the target is built, then it is each universe stock's residual return over the registered horizon after D, with factors fitted only on data up to D.

nodes.title: Information gain is measured as the out-of-sample improvement of a learned model with the feature over the same model without it.

criteria: Given a feature, when it is tested, then a model trained with it and one trained without it are compared on the HARN test period using a registered metric (such as the rank correlation of predicted and realised residual returns), and the difference is the feature's gain.

nodes.title: Every feature claim is tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill.

criteria: Given a feature's per-date gains on the held-out period, when it is tested, then the null-hypothesis-testing skill is given those gains and the count of every feature tried; the feature survives only if the null of zero gain is rejected at 5% after correction for that count.

nodes.title: The data behind each test is characterised with the data-analysis skill on the real data.

criteria: Given a feature test, when it is run, then the data-analysis skill reports the feature's distribution, missing share, stability across years and its correlation with the other candidates, on the real universe data.

nodes.title: Every feature's verdict is recorded, failed ones included.

criteria: Given a tested feature, when its verdict is decided, then the feature, its gain, the test result and the correction applied are recorded through HARN, and the list of survivors is saved as the stage S3 result.

nodes.title: Sequence models forecast each stock's forward return over registered horizons.

criteria: Given date D and a stock in D's universe, when a forecast is made, then the model reads the stock's history of the features that survived stage 3 (FTEST) over a fixed lookback ending at D and outputs its forward return for each registered horizon (by default 1, 5 and 21 trading days).

nodes.title: Sequence models forecast each stock's forward realised volatility over the same horizons.

criteria: Given date D, when a volatility forecast is made, then it is the realised volatility of daily returns over the h trading days after D, for each registered horizon.

nodes.title: Forecast inputs never reach past the forecast date.

criteria: Given a forecast made on D, when any input dated after D is changed, then the forecast is unchanged.

nodes.title: Return forecasts are compared with simple baselines.

criteria: Given the test period, when return forecasts are scored, then their rank correlation with realised returns is compared with that of a zero forecast and of the stock's own trailing mean; the claim passes only if the null-hypothesis-testing skill rejects the null of no improvement over the better baseline at 5% after correction for the number of models and horizons tried.

nodes.title: Volatility forecasts are compared with simple baselines.

criteria: Given the test period, when volatility forecasts are scored, then their error against realised volatility is compared with that of the trailing 21-day volatility and an exponentially weighted volatility; the claim passes only if the null-hypothesis-testing skill rejects the null of no improvement at 5% after correction.

nodes.title: Delisted stocks' final periods stay in the test.

criteria: Given a stock that delists within a forecast horizon, when its target is computed, then its realised return through delisting is used, not dropped.

nodes.title: Training can run on a rented graphics card and the results are brought back to the laptop.

criteria: Given a training run, when it runs on rented hardware, then its trained model, settings and seeds are saved so that forecasts and the HARN record are produced on the laptop.

nodes.title: Forecast-driven portfolios use the return forecasts with a covariance estimate from stage S2.

criteria: Given a rebalance date, when the portfolio is built, then its weights use the FCST return (and optionally volatility) forecasts with the best COV estimator, under the same long-only and 5%-per-stock limits as PORT.

nodes.title: Forecast-driven portfolios must beat the stage S2 benchmark out of sample after costs.

criteria: Given the HARN final test period and the 10 basis point cost, when each forecast-driven portfolio's Sharpe ratio after costs is compared with the PORT benchmark's, then it passes only if the null-hypothesis-testing skill rejects the null of no improvement at 5% after correction for every portfolio variant tried.

nodes.title: A loss is a recorded result.

criteria: Given a forecast-driven portfolio that fails to beat the benchmark, when the run ends, then the loss is recorded through HARN with its results and a written explanation.

nodes.title: The backtest environment replays the point-in-time universe day by day.

criteria: Given a training or test episode, when the agent acts on date D, then it sees only data known by D's close, its action sets portfolio weights for D+1, and the reward is the next day's portfolio return after the 10 basis point cost, less a risk penalty, so that the episode's total reward tracks its Sharpe ratio after costs.

nodes.title: The environment applies the same rules as every other portfolio.

criteria: Given an agent's weights, when they are applied, then they are long-only, fully invested (cash allowed), at most 5% per stock, and delisted stocks' final returns are realised.

nodes.title: Agents are trained by proximal policy optimisation.

criteria: Given a training run, when the policy is updated, then each update is limited by a clipped ratio between the new and old policy, using rewards collected in the backtest environment on the training period only.

nodes.title: Agents must beat the stage S2 benchmark out of sample after costs.

criteria: Given the HARN final test period, when each agent's Sharpe ratio after costs is compared with the PORT benchmark's, then it passes only if the null-hypothesis-testing skill rejects the null of no improvement at 5% after correction for every agent configuration tried.

nodes.title: Agent results are robust to training randomness.

criteria: Given an agent configuration, when it is trained with at least 5 different random seeds, then the verdict uses the results across all seeds, never the best one alone.

nodes.title: A loss is a recorded result.

criteria: Given an agent that fails to beat the benchmark, when the run ends, then the loss is recorded through HARN with its results and a written explanation.

nodes.title: Paper trading runs the stage S2 benchmark and every stage S4 strategy that passed its bar, forward from a start date.

criteria: Given a start date, when a new daily batch is accepted, then each paper-traded strategy's orders for the next day are generated from data known at that day's close, and filled at the next day's close with the 10 basis point cost.

nodes.title: Paper positions, trades and results are recorded daily and shown in the app.

criteria: Given a paper-traded strategy, when the researcher opens it in the app, then its positions, trades, daily return after costs and turnover since start are shown against the benchmark's.

nodes.title: Paper trading never contacts a broker.

criteria: Given any paper-trading run, when it runs, then no order is sent outside the laptop.

nodes.title: A paper strategy's settings are frozen at its start.

criteria: Given a paper-traded strategy, when it runs, then it uses the model and settings it started with; any change starts a new paper record.

nodes.title: Daily prices, corporate actions and company listings come from the existing Sharadar subscription.

criteria: Given a full build, when its sources are listed, then the primary data is from that subscription only.

nodes.title: The data covers every US common stock that traded since 2000-01-03, including those later delisted.

criteria: Given any date from 2000-01-03, when the stored listings are checked, then they include stocks that delisted after that date, and the build report states the count of delisted stocks per year.

nodes.title: Splits, dividends, ticker changes and delistings are present with their effective dates.

criteria: Given a stock with a known split, when its adjusted prices are loaded, then there is no jump at the split date larger than the day's real move.

nodes.title: Each stored value carries the date it became known.

criteria: Given any stored row, when it is inspected, then it carries the date it was first published and, if corrected, the date of each correction.

nodes.title: A second independent daily price source is available for cross-checking.

criteria: Given the cross-check, when it runs, then its prices and corporate actions come from a source independent of the primary subscription.

nodes.title: For the fallback universe, historical S&P 500 membership by date is available.

criteria: Given the fallback universe is used, when membership for any date is needed, then the members on that date, including later-removed ones, are available.

nodes.title: Everything runs on one laptop, except optional neural network training on rented hardware.

criteria: A full build, the stage S2 comparison and the stage S3 feature tests each complete on the laptop; only FCST and AGENT training may use rented hardware.

nodes.title: The full dataset fits on the laptop.

criteria: The stored dataset for 1,000 universe stocks over 25 years, with all listings, takes ≤ 20 GB of disk, and loading 25 years of universe returns takes ≤ 30 seconds and ≤ 8 GB of memory.

nodes.title: An incremental daily update completes in ≤ 10 minutes, cross-check included.

criteria: Timed on the laptop on a normal trading-day update.

nodes.title: Data costs nothing beyond the existing subscription and a free second source.

criteria: The architecture lists every paid service; the only one is the existing subscription (and rented graphics hardware per QR-05).

nodes.title: Rented graphics hardware costs at most $10 per training run.

criteria: Each FCST or AGENT training run states its expected hours and cost before it starts, and the expected cost is ≤ $10.

nodes.title: The app is reachable only from the laptop itself.

criteria: Opening the app from another device on the same network fails.

nodes.title: Subscription credentials are never shown in full or stored in the project's history.

criteria: A search of the project's committed files and logs finds no credential.
